officialSummary: The Reserve Bank of India has launched the 75th round of its Order Books, Inventories and Capacity Utilisation Survey (OBICUS). The survey is for the reference period July – September 2026 (Q2:2026-27). The Reserve Bank has been conducting the Order Books, Inventories and Capacity Utilisation Survey (OBICUS) of the manufacturing sector on a quarterly basis since 2008. The information collected in the survey includes quantitative data on new orders received during the reference quarter, backlog of orders at the beginning of the quarter, pending orders at the end of the quarter, total inventories with a breakup between ﬁnished goods (FG), work-in-progress (WiP) and raw material (RM) inventories at the end of the quarter, item-wise production in terms of quantity and value during the quarter vis-à-vis the installed capacity from the targeted group and the reasons for changes in production / installed capacity during the quarter. The level of capacity utilisation (CU) is estimated from these responses. The survey provides valuable input for monetary policy formulation. The survey findings are released on the website of the Bank regularly. During this quarter, selected manufacturing companies will be approached by the Bank. Other manufacturing companies may also participate in the survey by downloading the survey questionnaire from the Reserve Bank’s website https://www.rbi.org.in/ . The survey questionnaire is placed under the head ‘ Forms ’ (available under the ‘More Links’ at the bottom of the home page) and sub-head ‘ Survey ’. The duly authenticated filled-in survey schedule may be e-mailed as per contact details provided in the survey schedule. Company level data are treated as confidential and never disclosed. In case of any query/clarification, kindly contact us at the following address: The Director, Division of Enterprise Surveys, Department of Statistics and Information Management, Reserve Bank of India, C-8, 2nd floor, Bandra-Kurla Complex, Bandra (East), Mum
title: RBI launches Quarterly Order Books, Inventories and Capacity Utilisation Survey: July – September 2026 (Round 75)

officialSummary: Today the Reserve Bank of India placed on its website a Working Paper titled, “ Data Gaps in State-Level Inflation: An Assessment for the Covid Period ” under the Reserve Bank of India Working Paper Series 1 . The paper is co-authored by Purnima Shaw and R. K. Sinha. The collection and compilation of official statistics was affected during the outbreak of Covid-19 pandemic due to the resulting restrictions across the world. In India, imputed price indices for the official inflation were released at the aggregate level for the months of April and May 2020. However, the State-wise official inflation figures remain unavailable for four of the pandemic months viz., April and May 2020 and April and May 2021. In this context, this paper uses RBI’s Inflation Expectations Survey of Households (IESH) granular data to derive State-wise CPI-U inflation estimates for these four pandemic months. The paper describes the importance of IESH, which continued to be conducted bimonthly and disseminated during the pandemic months. Using the distributions of centre-wise urban consumers’ inflation perceptions, three months ahead inflation expectations, and past State-wise realised CPI-U inflation figures, the paper derives estimates for the State-wise official inflation pertaining to the specified Covid months. These State-wise inflation estimates when aggregated, closely follow the all-India official CPI inflation series. State-wise inflation data are crucial in the current inflation targeting regime, and therefore, providing estimates for the specific months (for which the official CPI data remains unpublished) can be potentially useful for future research involving State-level inflation time-series data. (Brij Raj) Chief General Manager Press Release: 2026-2027/1298 1 The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) introduced the RBI Working Papers series in March 2011.
